name: Skyroot Aerospace
one_liner: Hyderabad startup building the Vikram family of small-satellite rockets; flew India's first private rocket (2022) and first private orbital launch (2026).
story: Founded in 2018 by former ISRO scientists Pawan Kumar Chandana and Naga Bharath Daka, Skyroot bet that a private company could build orbital rockets in a country where launch had been an ISRO monopoly; its suborbital Vikram-S became India's first privately built rocket to fly in November 2022. A $60M round co-led by GIC and Sherpalo in May 2026 valued it at about $1.1B (reported as pre-money; ~$160M raised in total), and on 18 July 2026 Vikram-1 reached orbit on its maiden flight, the first private orbital launch from India. The 2023 Temasek round was a pre-Series C (mapped to C); the Series A amount ($11M) comes from an Entrackr funding tally.

name: Agnikul Cosmos
one_liner: IIT Madras-incubated rocket startup flying the Agnibaan launcher on Agnilet, the world's first single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine.
story: Agnikul, incubated at IIT Madras's National Centre for Combustion R&D in Chennai and led by co-founder/CEO Srinath Ravichandran, bet that an entire rocket engine could be 3D-printed as a single piece. On 30 May 2024 its Agnibaan SOrTeD flew from India's first private launchpad after a run of scrubs since March (one 28 May attempt was called off seconds before lift-off), which ISRO called the first controlled flight of an additively manufactured semi-cryogenic engine. A ~Rs150 crore (~$17M) round in November 2025 valued it at $500M; total raised is reported as over $78M by Inc42 (CB Insights lists ~$61M).

near_death.what: Agnibaan SOrTeD launch scrubbed repeatedly from March to May 2024 (including a 28 May abort less than a minute before lift-off) before flying on the fifth attempt on 30 May.
